claim_text: FBR's tax-to-GDP ratio reached 10.3% in FY2024-25 up from 8.8% in FY2023-24
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: Total FBR net tax collection was Rs 11744.3 billion in FY2024-25 up 26.3% YoY from Rs 9299.1 billion
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: Direct taxes were Rs 5791.7 billion = 49.3% of total FBR collection in FY2024-25
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: Indirect taxes were Rs 5952.6 billion = 50.7% of total FBR collection in FY2024-25
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: Sales tax collection was Rs 3901.4 billion = 33.2% of total FBR collection in FY2024-25
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: Customs duty collection was Rs 1284.6 billion = 10.9% of total FBR collection in FY2024-25
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: Federal Excise Duty collection was Rs 766.6 billion = 6.5% of total FBR collection in FY2024-25
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: Withholding tax collection was Rs 3381.5 billion in FY2024-25 equal to 59% of income tax collection and 28.8% of total FBR collection
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: Income tax composition FY2024-25 was withholding tax 59% advance tax 33% and collection on demand (arrears) 5% up from 3% the prior year
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: By subtraction only approximately 3% of income tax collected in FY2024-25 was paid voluntarily with a filed return rather than withheld advance or enforced

claim_text: Salary withholding tax collection rose from Rs 391.4 billion in FY2023-24 to Rs 605.6 billion in FY2024-25 a 54.7% increase
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25 Table 8

claim_text: Contracts withholding tax collection was Rs 737.7 billion in FY2024-25 up 39.0% from Rs 530.7 billion
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25 Table 8

claim_text: Domestic-stage tax collection rose from 63.6% of total FBR collection in FY2023-24 to 64.8% in FY2024-25
source: FBR Revenue Division Year Book 2024-25

claim_text: Taxes on income profits and capital gains were the largest category of Pakistan's tax revenue in 2023 at 40.7% of total tax revenue

claim_text: Under the 7th NFC Award 2010 provinces receive 57.5% of the federal divisible pool (56% in 2010-11) and the federal government retains 42.5%
source: 7th National Finance Commission Award 2010

claim_text: The horizontal NFC distribution formula weights population 82% poverty/backwardness 10.3% revenue collection 5% and inverse population density 2.7%
source: 7th National Finance Commission Award 2010

claim_text: Provincial shares of the NFC divisible pool are Punjab 51.74% Sindh 24.55% Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 14.62% and Balochistan 9.09%
source: 7th National Finance Commission Award 2010

claim_text: FBR's collection charge on the divisible pool was cut from 5% to 1% under the 7th NFC Award enlarging the distributable pool
source: 7th National Finance Commission Award 2010

claim_text: 1% of the net divisible pool was earmarked for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as a frontline province in the war on terror
source: 7th National Finance Commission Award 2010

claim_text: No NFC award has superseded the 7th NFC Award since 2010 and its formula remains current in 2026; the 8th NFC (constituted 2010) produced no award and the 9th NFC was constituted in April 2015
source: Dawn / PIDE / SDPI / Wikipedia National Finance Commission Award entry for historical sequence; current-in-2026 status confirmed by production team 2026-08-28

claim_text: FBR retained income tax on non-agricultural income sales tax on goods customs duty and federal excise duty after the 18th Amendment

claim_text: Tax Laws (Amendment) Act 2024 / Finance Act 2025 Section 114C defines eligible and ineligible persons and restricts banking property vehicle and securities transactions for ineligible (non-filer) persons
source: Business Recorder / PropPakistani / Express Tribune / 24NewsHD coverage of Tax Laws Amendment Bill 2024

claim_text: Section 114C implementation was deferred by the National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance in early 2025 pending FBR system readiness before being folded into the FY2025-26 Finance Bill

claim_text: Extent of actual 2026 enforcement of Section 114C non-filer restrictions at scale is unconfirmed by a primary FBR enforcement statistic

claim_text: Stated government rationale for filer/non-filer restrictions is to broaden the tax base increase documentation and discourage staying outside the formal tax net
source: PropPakistani and other press coverage quoting government officials
